transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-03
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alice Chen (Redwood AE), Ben Park (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Redwood Product), Raj Patel (Aperture ML), Sofia Morales (Aperture CTO), Evan Reed (Aperture Infra)

Summary:
Quick Optimize walkthrough focusing on INT8 vs FP8 quantization profiles, expected latency/throughput gains, and observed quality regressions on representative prompt sets. Customer is evaluating cost savings for production inference and wants a pilot comparing INT8 (8-bit) and mixed FP8 options.

Topics Covered:
- Overview of Redwood Optimize quantization profiles
- Benchmarks: latency, tokens/sec, token-cost tradeoffs
- Quality vs latency comparisons and how we run regressions/auto-evals
- Pilot scoping and next steps (data, prompts, metrics)

Transcript:
[00:00] Alice Chen: hey everybody thanks for joining, i think we have about 45 minutes, i'll run quick agenda, ben is gonna walk through the optimize quant profiles and then we'll leave time for q's and pilot scoping.
[00:08] Raj Patel: sounds good thanks alice.
[00:12] Ben Park: alright um so i'll share my screen, if you can't see shout out, ok focusing on two main profiles int8 and fp8 (we sometimes say f p eight), and a baseline fp16 run. the main tradeoffs: int8 gives biggest cost drop, fp8 is often a middle ground with slightly better quality but similar cost to int8 depending on hardware.
[00:35] Sofia Morales: quick q, is fp8 widely supported across GPUs? like on our dedicated clusters?
[00:40] Ben Park: great question, fp8 support depends on the runtime and vendor kernels; with our hosted fleet we support fp8 on A100x and H100 where vendor kernels exist; for dedicated/private we validate kernel availability during onboarding — sometimes we fall back to mixed-precision emulation which reduces gains.
[01:00] Evan Reed: noted, we run mostly A100s in prod, a few T4s for cheaper inference. how much of a perf delta should i expect?
[01:08] Ben Park: empirically on A100 fp16 -> int8 gives ~2.5-4x token/sec improvement for generative workloads with small to medium sequences, latency often drops ~30-60% for tail p99 depending on batching; fp8 sits between fp16 and int8 on quality and latency in many tests. caveat: it depends on KV cache usage and sequence length distribution — for long-form generation the delta can shift.
[01:35] Raj Patel: when you say quality, what metrics do you use? are we looking at perplexity, BLEU, or human evals?
[01:42] Ben Park: we do a layered approach: automatic metrics (perplexity, embedding-similarity vs baseline outputs, ngram overlap) plus a small human eval on critical prompts. Redwood Optimize ties regressions to prompt sets so you can see where token-level odds changed and surface semantic drift. our experience: some models are very robust to int8, others show subtle hallucination increases on edge prompts.
[02:05] Sofia Morales: can you show an example where int8 failed vs fp8?
[02:10] Ben Park: yep, on a financial calculation prompt we saw int8 produce numeric rounding errors more often; fp8 preserved numerics better. i'll pull a quick example — (screen noise) — here: baseline fp16 answer: 'Total: $12,345.67' int8: 'Total: $12,300.00' fp8: 'Total: $12,345.60' — small but for finance it's material.
[02:42] Raj Patel: ok that's helpful. what about latency vs throughput tradeoff if we enable prefix caching?
[02:48] Ben Park: prefix/KV caching benefits all precisions — it reduces cold-start tokens and repeated context cost. int8 with caching yields especially strong per-token cost wins. however, for single-request tail latency, batching and scheduling influence p95/p99 more than quant alone.
[03:05] Alice Chen: i'll add that our Console shows per-token latency and cost breakdowns by profile, so you can compare side-by-side over your traffic patterns.
[03:14] Sofia Morales: nice. any caveats for sampling/temperature changes? like does int8 change distribution of outputs at higher temps?
[03:20] Ben Park: yes sometimes sampling variance grows slightly at high temperature; we recommend re-running your calibration prompts at the intended sampling settings. Optimize supports sampling-aware regressions so you can test temperature 0.7 vs 1.0 etc.
[03:35] Evan Reed: what about model types — decoder-only vs encoder-decoder?
[03:39] Ben Park: most of our quant profiles are optimized for decoder-only generative models; encoder-decoder behavior is generally similar but you should always run your end-to-end evals.
[03:48] Raj Patel: can you outline the pilot we'd run? what data do you need from us?
[03:54] Alice Chen: sure, typical pilot: 1) provide 2-3 representative prompt sets (we asked for 3), 2) baseline fp16 run from your current infra or ours, 3) run INT8 and FP8 profiles on same model versions and collect metrics (latency, tokens/sec, cost, automated regressions), 4) a small human eval slice for high-risk prompts. Ben will propose config.
[04:18] Ben Park: to add: we'll run the profiles on both hosted and dedicated analogs if you want to see the delta between our hosted fleet and your Dedicated config. need to confirm quota and GPU availability for pilot window.
[04:30] Sofia Morales: what's the expected cost savings? "ballpark" is fine.
[04:34] Ben Park: ballpark is model-dependent; we've seen 30-70% per-token cost reduction with int8 vs fp16 when accounting for throughput improvements; fp8 is closer to 40-60%. again depends on kernel support and batching.
[04:50] Raj Patel: any impact on safety filters/moderation?
[04:53] Maya Singh: we run moderation on outputs post-decode; quantization shouldn't change the moderation pipeline itself but if outputs shift meaningfully it could affect false positives/negatives. that's why we include safety prompts in the eval set.
[05:08] Sofia Morales: can we set thresholds so the system rejects an optimized profile if quality regression exceeds X%?
[05:12] Ben Park: yes, Optimize supports fail-fast criteria: you define a regression tolerance per-metric and per-prompt-set; if the profile crosses the threshold we won't promote it to production routes.
[05:22] Evan Reed: operationally how do we roll this out? can we do a canary to 5% traffic?
[05:27] Alice Chen: absolutely — Console supports canary rollouts by route and model profile. you can route 5% to int8, 95% to baseline, and toggle auto-fallback.
[05:36] Raj Patel: about fp8 naming — i've seen e4m vs e5m in kernels, is that relevant?
[05:40] Ben Park: kernel naming varies by vendor, but we surface compatibility matrix in onboarding docs. we'll verify kernel compatibility with your infra.
[05:46] Sofia Morales: are there risks around reproducibility? we need deterministic outputs for some use cases.
[05:50] Ben Park: quantization can introduce non-determinism across runs due to low precision math and different kernel implementations. for strict determinism we advise pinned fp16 or deterministic infer paths; Optimize can also run repeated seeds to estimate variance.
[06:05] Raj Patel: can you run a quick demo in the Console comparing profiles?
[06:09] Ben Park: sure i'll switch to the Console — (screen share) — top-left is model catalog, i've selected the model, profile tab shows fp16 baseline, int8-s8 (our label), and fp8-mix. here you can see metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, and a quality delta column.
[06:33] Ben Park: i'll kick off a small benchmark using your sample prompts (we loaded the provided 30 prompts), starting with fp16 baseline — running... (wait) — baseline avg latency 210ms p50, p95 480ms, tokens/sec 780.
[06:50] Ben Park: now int8 run... int8 p50 120ms, p95 220ms, tokens/sec 2100. fp8 run coming up... fp8 p50 140ms p95 300ms tokens/sec 1600.
[07:05] Sofia Morales: that's a pretty big boost. are those numbers per GPU?
[07:09] Ben Park: yes these are per-worker numbers with our batching settings, can vary by instance size.
[07:14] Raj Patel: show me the quality delta column.
[07:17] Ben Park: here: most prompts are green (<1% embedding distance), but three prompts flagged: #7 numeric calc, #19 legal style, #23 factual recall — int8 showed larger embedding drift on 19 and 23. fp8 had smaller drift on 23 but still a small delta on 19.
[07:33] Raj Patel: what's the embedding metric threshold you use?
[07:36] Ben Park: by default we flag >0.12 cosine distance change vs baseline, but that's configurable.
[07:42] Sofia Morales: can we see the raw outputs side-by-side?
[07:45] Ben Park: yes side-by-side viewer — here are fp16 / fp8 / int8 outputs for prompt 19 — you can toggle token alignments; note transcription quirk: sometimes tokens are mis-aligned in the UI for mixed kernels (we have a fix in the next release).
[08:00] Raj Patel: okay, that helps. how long does a full regression suite usually take?
[08:04] Ben Park: for 500 prompts it's typically 1-2 hours on our benchmark pool; for larger suites we recommend overnight runs.
[08:10] Evan Reed: are there any data residency or logs differences when using Optimize on Dedicated vs Hosted?
[08:14] Alice Chen: Dedicated keeps logs in your VPC (or on-prem) per the Private deployment model; hosted stores logs per your retention settings in the console but you can integrate with your SIEM and export. we'll share the SOC2 / KMS docs.
[08:29] Sofia Morales: what about model variance with streaming responses? any issues with quant?
[08:33] Ben Park: streaming is sensitive to kernel buffering, but we've tuned streaming for int8; however p99 token latency can still be impacted by scheduling. if you rely on strict streaming timing we recommend a test run.
[08:47] Raj Patel: could you explain briefly how you build the int8 profile — is it post-training quantization, or using quant-aware finetune?
[08:53] Ben Park: our int8 is typically a post-training quantization with per-channel scales and some ops left in higher precision as needed; for high-risk workloads we recommend quant-aware finetune or calibration with representative data. Optimize includes a calibration step that can help.
[09:07] Sofia Morales: does that require us to share training data?
[09:10] Ben Park: calibration uses only representative prompts/contexts, not training corpora. for quant-aware finetune we'd need training data but it's optional.
[09:17] Raj Patel: your earlier example of numerical errors — can calibration fix that?
[09:21] Ben Park: sometimes calibration reduces numeric drift by tuning scales; other times you need to keep certain layers in fp16. Optimize's profile editor lets you pin ops to higher precision.
[09:33] Alice Chen: quick note on observability: you'll get per-route cost estimates and token-level attribution so you can see which customers or endpoints drive variance.
[09:43] Sofia Morales: OK let's talk about success criteria for us — what would make the pilot a go/no-go?
[09:48] Raj Patel: for us: 1) maintain semantic accuracy on core prompts (<2% human-detected regression), 2) reduce per-token cost by >=40%, 3) p95 latency improvement >=25%.
[09:59] Ben Park: those are reasonable; we'll configure the pilot to evaluate against those thresholds.
[10:05] Maya Singh: want to mention fallback policies — if a profile fails quality checks in production we auto-fallback to baseline and alert.
[10:12] Raj Patel: good. any security or audit items we should be aware of before pilot?
[10:17] Alice Chen: we'll send the security pack: SOC2, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS integration notes, and audit log samples. put a note that Dedicated keeps logs in your account.
[10:28] Evan Reed: timeline: we want to start pilot next week if possible.
[10:31] Ben Park: we can provision a pilot window next Tue-Wed, need your prompts and confirmation on model version.
[10:36] Raj Patel: i'll send prompt sets by Friday.
[10:38] Sofia Morales: and pricing? do we get a pilot discount?
[10:41] Alice Chen: yes pilots are usually complimentary for the benchmarking hours; after pilot Ben will share cost estimates for production.
[10:48] Raj Patel: are there any legal hoops for pilot? like data processing agreement?
[10:52] Alice Chen: standard DPA applies for hosted; for Dedicated/Private we can discuss a short-term addendum — legal can follow up.
[10:58] Sofia Morales: ok last q — can you compare int8 vs fp8 for hallucination rates specifically?
[11:04] Ben Park: we track hallucination proxies (fact-error detection, citation mismatch) — across many models int8 slightly increases hallucination on low-context factual prompts, fp8 reduces that gap often by half relative to int8. but results are model & prompt specific.
[11:20] Raj Patel: good to know. any final notes on ergonomics?
[11:23] Ben Park: Optimize profile editor is low-code: you can tweak layer precision, calibration settings, and promotion rules. we'll include a runbook for pilot ops.
[11:33] (crosstalk)
[11:35] Alice Chen: wrap-up and next steps: alice to send spreadsheet and security pack, ben to send pilot config and cost estimate, raj to send prompts. schedule: pilot kickoff Tuesday.
[11:48] Sofia Morales: thanks everyone this was helpful.
[11:51] Raj Patel: thanks.

Notes / imperfections: transcription sometimes shows 'f p eight' instead of 'fp8', 'K V cache' instead of KV cache, and occasional word swaps (e.g., 'hosted' -> 'hasted'). speaker labels are accurate except for a couple short interruptions.

End of transcript.
